summary: All 13 quoted Scriptures (Jonah 1:2, 1:9, 1:12, 1:15, 1:17, 2:2, 2:4, 2:6, 2:9, 2:10 and Matthew 12:39-41) are KJV-verbatim, every narrative fact matches Jonah 1-4, and the substitution/resurrection doctrine soundly lands on Christ with a grace-anchored, fear-free CTA.

findings.quote_or_claim: the seat of the people who slaughtered mine ... the very people who had butchered mine
findings.problem: Interpretive backstory not stated in the book of Jonah (and arguably anachronistic, since Assyria's major destruction of Israel post-dates Jonah son of Amittai's ministry). It does NOT contradict the text — it is a defensible, historically-grounded homiletic motivation for Jonah's flight, and the narration correctly grounds his actual stated reason in Jonah 4:2 ('I knew Him to be gracious and slow to anger'). Noted for transparency only; does not force a FIX.
findings.proposed_fix_text: (optional, if tightening to text) the great and cruel city of my enemies
